title: Decide whether AI is the right solution
summary: AI is powerful but costly, unpredictable and sometimes unnecessary. Check that AI is the best way to solve the user's problem before committing to it.

beginner: Write the user problem without mentioning AI.
List simpler options: rules, better design, search or a manual process.
Ask where AI would add real value: handling variety, scale or language that rules cannot.
Ask what happens when the AI is wrong, and how bad that would be.
Estimate the running cost per use.
Decide and record why AI is, or is not, the right choice.
intermediate: Compare AI with non-AI options on value, cost and risk.
Assess the cost of errors and the need for human review.
Record the decision and the evidence.
experienced: Check the AI approach creates lasting advantage, not just novelty.
Assess build, buy or partner options.
Agree quality and cost thresholds before committing.

toolExamples.claude: Prototype the AI part quickly with a handful of real examples to see if quality is close to good enough.

definitionOfDone: Cost of errors and running cost assessed
pitfalls: Underestimating the impact of wrong answers
